subject.title: feat(ui): approval UX overhaul — inline cards, fair queue, shortcuts, badges

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this multi-surface core Control UI approval-workflow redesign after its safety defects and runtime proof are resolved?
rationale: The change adds a large permanent approval interaction model—queue ordering, inline placement, shortcuts, and navigation indicators—rather than repairing a documented broken contract; the protected maintainer label also requires explicit human handling.

options.title: Sponsor and narrow the redesign
options.body: Keep the direction, require the identified approval-safety fixes and real Control UI proof, then review the resulting scoped UX contract.

options.title: Reduce to a smaller approval improvement
options.body: Retain only the most valuable bounded improvement, such as fair queue ordering, and defer inline cards, shortcuts, and sidebar indicators to a separately approved design.

options.title: Pause the feature direction
options.body: Close or defer the PR if OpenClaw does not want a core-owned approval UX expansion at this time.

recommendation.title: Sponsor and narrow the redesign
recommendation.body: Keep the direction, require the identified approval-safety fixes and real Control UI proof, then review the resulting scoped UX contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The timeline assigns this PR to steipete and the branch commits show direct ownership of the proposed interaction model.
